drug_class: Topical corticosteroid (steroid cream/ointment/tape applied to the skin)
purpose: Flurandrenolide is used to reduce redness, swelling, itching, and irritation caused by certain skin conditions like eczema, psoriasis, or allergic skin reactions. It helps calm down inflammation on the skin. Your doctor may prescribe it to relieve discomfort and help your skin heal.
how_it_works: This medication is a mild steroid that you apply directly to your skin. It works by calming down the immune response in your skin that causes redness, itching, and swelling. Think of it as turning down the volume on your skin's overactive inflammation response.
common_side_effects: Burning, stinging, or itching at the spot where you apply it. You may also notice some skin dryness, redness, or mild irritation. With long-term use, the skin can become thin, develop stretch marks, or show small broken blood vessels. These effects are more likely if you use it on large areas or for a long time.
warnings: Do not use this on your face, underarms, or groin unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Do not cover the treated area with tight bandages or plastic wrap unless directed, as this can increase absorption and side effects. Keep it away from your eyes. Do not use it on infected skin without treating the infection first. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding before using this medication.
typical_dosing: Usually applied to the affected skin area one to three times per day, or as directed by your doctor. Use only a thin layer and rub it in gently. Do not use more than prescribed, and do not use it for longer than recommended — typically no more than a few weeks unless your doctor advises otherwise.
